Somebody told me you are fixing up an old house. How long have you been at it?
Since 2021. I have been restoring it room by room, and I am nowhere near done.
Four years. Wow. What have you actually finished?
Two bedrooms and the kitchen. The floor took months — it was painstaking. But we salvaged the original wood, so it was worth it.
You clearly have a knack for this. Did you learn it somewhere?
Nowhere. I have always been into old things. I just started, and I have been learning by ruining things ever since.
And what is left? What have you been putting off?
The hallway. I have never gotten around to painting it. Four years of walking past it. It is a labor of love, Dave, not a schedule.
So far I have finished the kitchen and both bedrooms.
How long have you been working on that?
I have known my neighbor for six years.
Honestly, it is a labor of love.

People ask me how long I have been working on the house, and I always laugh, because the honest answer is nine years. Nine years for one house. When we bought it, the roof was worn out, the windows did not close, and there was carpet glued to a wooden floor that turned out to be beautiful underneath. I have finished the kitchen and both bedrooms. I have been working on the staircase since March and it is still not done. My husband says it is a labor of love, and he is right, although some weekends it feels like just labor. What I have learned is that you never restore a house. The house restores you. I am far more patient than I was nine years ago, and I have a knack for things I did not even know I could do.

My wife has been asking me the same question every Saturday for about three years. How long have you been out there? And the honest answer is usually four hours. I go into the garage to fix one thing and I come out at dinner time. I have always been into old radios. Not collecting them, mind you, repairing them. I have fixed maybe forty of them and I have given away almost all of them. People think it must be relaxing. It is not relaxing at all. It is painstaking, and half the parts do not exist anymore, so you salvage what you can. But when a radio that has been silent for sixty years starts playing, there is nothing like it. That is why I have never gotten around to selling any of them.
